facts.text: St. Marks’ Mark Catholic Church, built 1903‑1906, showcases Romanesque Revival style using limestone from a Wichita factory and stained‑glass windows shipped from Germany.
German Catholic immigrants from Luxembourg and the Rhineland founded St. Marks in the early 1870s, drawn by the Homestead Act and escape from religious persecution.
During World War II, parishioners built the Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto over 50 years ago, collecting stones by Monsignor John Hackenbroich to honor Marian devotions.
The town’s first post office, opened in February 1879 by postmaster Anton Kasmirski, served families until its closure on December 14, 1903.
Consecrated in 1906 by Bishop Thomas Hennessy before 2,000–3,000, Mark Catholic Church became the first Sedgwick County site on the National Register of Historic Places outside Wichita in 1991.
St. Marks celebrated its parish’s 125th anniversary in 2000 and added a Parish Life Center in 2003, preserving its immigrant roots amid Wichita’s growth.
